MALA Framework: A Framework for Multi-Agent AI Integration in Legacy Industrial Systems

This work introduces MALA (Multi Agent Legacy Architecture), a supervised multi-agent framework designed for industrial environments operating on heterogeneous legacy systems that lack modern APIs.

Research Overview

Many industrial environments continue to rely on terminal-based enterprise systems, flat-file archives, scanned documents, and local operational logs accumulated over decades. These systems often expose limited interoperability and present barriers to contemporary AI integration.

MALA proposes a three-tier architecture for grounded AI-assisted decision support in such settings. Rather than replacing legacy software, the framework treats existing industrial systems as operational surfaces and integrates:



Gatherer Agents implementing Recursive Context Enrichment (RCE) to collect and normalize evidence across heterogeneous sources.

Critic Agents enforcing deterministic safety constraints through a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) formulation.

Human-on-the-Loop (HotL) oversight for escalation, exception handling, and verification of medium-confidence or high-risk actions.


The framework incorporates freshness-aware retrieval, evidence traceability, confidence-based escalation, ontological mapping of local industrial terminology, and auditable workflow logging for supervised deployment in industrial contexts.

Evaluation Summary

The accompanying study evaluates MALA using a retrospective replay and shadow-execution protocol on archived disruption-management cycles from a legacy European steel-production environment. The evaluation focuses on supervised decision support under matched evidence conditions and explicitly excludes autonomous live deployment.

Across a 50-cycle replay dataset, the framework demonstrated:



Reduced decision-support latency relative to manual workflows.

Zero recorded safety violations under CMDP-constrained execution.

Limited Human-on-the-Loop intervention requirements.

Improved task success relative to unconstrained fully agentic baselines.


The study additionally includes ablation analysis, threshold sensitivity experiments, grounded case-trace evaluation, and deployment-oriented discussion for industrial legacy modernization contexts.

Repository Contents

This archive may include:



Research manuscript and supplementary material.

Reference implementation of the MALA framework.

Example orchestration and safety-control modules.

Experimental configurations and replay methodology.

Documentation for reproducibility and future extensions.


Important Notes



Research status: Preprint / independent research artifact.

Evaluation mode: Retrospective replay and shadow execution. No autonomous live plant actuation was performed.

Industrial data: Any operational data included in this archive has been anonymized or abstracted where required.

Intended audience: Researchers and practitioners in industrial AI, multi-agent systems, legacy modernization, human-AI collaboration, and safe autonomous systems.


Keywords

Multi-Agent Systems; Industrial AI; Legacy Systems; Human-on-the-Loop; CMDP Safety; Recursive Context Enrichment; AI for Manufacturing; Legacy Modernization; Explainable AI; Industrial Decision Support

titles.title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents

descriptions.description: Autonomous agents have long been a prominent research focus in both academic and industry communities. Previous research in this field often focuses on training agents with limited knowledge within isolated environments, which diverges significantly from human learning processes, and thus makes the agents hard to achieve human-like decisions. Recently, through the acquisition of vast amounts of web knowledge, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable potential in achieving human-level intelligence. This has sparked an upsurge in studies investigating LLM-based autonomous agents. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of these studies, delivering a systematic review of the field of LLM-based autonomous agents from a holistic perspective. More specifically, we first discuss the construction of LLM-based autonomous agents, for which we propose a unified framework that encompasses a majority of the previous work. Then, we present a comprehensive overview of the diverse applications of LLM-based autonomous agents in the fields of social science, natural science, and engineering. Finally, we delve into the evaluation strategies commonly used for LLM-based autonomous agents. Based on the previous studies, we also present several challenges and future directions in this field. To keep track of this field and continuously update our survey, we maintain a repository of relevant references at https://github.com/Paitesanshi/LLM-Agent-Survey.
Correcting several typos, 35 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables
